write.modelAfterSubmit: E-wallet apps have made it easier for teenagers to track where their pocket money goes. Although some people worry that these apps make spending too easy, their records can actually help young people manage their money better. Every payment made through an e-wallet is recorded automatically, and many apps show a weekly chart of where the money has gone. A student who checks this chart is likely to notice small habits that add up, such as buying bubble tea every afternoon. For example, my classmate Lan saw that snacks took up most of her spending last month, so she set a weekly limit in the app. However, the record only helps teenagers who actually look at it; otherwise, they may simply spend more without noticing.
